units.source_text: 我和护士一起给父亲换了冰水枕，然后把装好新冰块的冰袋敷在他的额头上。

en.t: Together with the nurse, I changed Father's ice-water pillow, then placed an ice bag filled with fresh ice on his forehead.

units.source_text: 我在父亲光秃的额头旁边，轻柔地用手按平装在冰袋里的尖利的碎冰。

en.t: Beside Father's bare forehead, I gently pressed down with my hand on the sharp broken ice inside the ice bag to smooth it flat.

units.source_text: 这时，哥哥从走廊进来，一声不吭地把一个邮件递给了我。

en.t: Just then, my elder brother came in from the corridor and silently handed me a piece of mail.

units.source_text: 我伸出闲着的左手接过这个邮件时，不禁觉得很奇怪。

en.t: When I reached out with my free left hand and took the mail, I could not help feeling puzzled.

units.source_text: 这个邮件比一般的信要沉得多，它不是装在一般的信封里，况且也不是一般信封能装得下的。

en.t: This piece of mail was much heavier than an ordinary letter; it was not in an ordinary envelope, and in any case it was too bulky to fit in one.

units.source_text: 它是用半纸包着的，封口用浆糊粘得很结实。

en.t: It was wrapped in hanshi paper, and the sealed edge had been firmly pasted shut with glue.

units.source_text: 我从哥哥手里接过来时，就发现这是一封挂号信。

en.t: When I took it from my brother's hand, I realized at once that it was a registered letter.

units.source_text: 翻过来一看，背面字迹工整地写着先生的名字。

en.t: When I turned it over and looked, Sensei's name was written neatly on the back.

units.source_text: 由于手占着，不能马上拆开看信，我就把它先揣进了怀里。

en.t: Because my hands were occupied and I could not open it at once to read it, I tucked it into my breast for the time being.

units.source_text: 1.半纸：日本一种写信习字用的纸。

en.t: 1. Hanshi: a type of Japanese paper used for writing letters and practicing calligraphy.
